query: To explain the transient epidermal hyperproliferation of the Col17a1−/− neonatal IFE, we exploited an in silico model (Kobayashi et al., 2016) to recapitulate the epidermal development. As COL17 serves as a linker between the epidermis and dermis and is expressed in basal cells, most of which are committed progenitor cells in the epidermis (Doupé and Jones, 2012; Lim et al., 2013), epidermal thickness was calculated upon the loosening of the attachment of committed progenitor cells to the BMZ. In the model with diminished adhesion, the epidermal thickness was transiently increased and gradually returned to the baseline (Figure 1f), which was compatible with the experimental observations of Col17a1−/− neonates and with the transient hypertrophy of Itga6- and Itgb1-null epidermis (Brakebusch et al., 2000; Niculescu et al., 2011).
